questions.questionText: What are the two stages of a RAG pipeline?
options: Retrieve relevant chunks for the query, then generate an answer using the query plus those chunks
questions.correctAnswer: Retrieve relevant chunks for the query, then generate an answer using the query plus those chunks
questions.explanation: RAG's entire idea is these two stages: a retrieval step that finds relevant context, and a generation step that answers using that context.

questions.questionText: Why can't you just paste an entire large knowledge base directly into every prompt instead of using retrieval?
options: You always can, retrieval offers no advantage
Context windows are finite, and most real knowledge bases are far larger than any context window regardless
LLMs cannot process more than one document at a time
Retrieval is only needed for very small knowledge bases
questions.correctAnswer: Context windows are finite, and most real knowledge bases are far larger than any context window regardless
questions.explanation: The context window's hard limit (context engineering lesson) is exactly what makes retrieving only the relevant subset necessary for any knowledge base of meaningful size.

questions.questionText: How does RAG help reduce hallucination compared to a model answering purely from its trained-in knowledge?
options: It doesn't affect hallucination at all
A model instructed to answer only from provided, retrieved context has much less room to confidently make something up than one relying on parametric memory alone
RAG makes the model larger, which prevents hallucination
RAG only works for models that have never hallucinated before
questions.correctAnswer: A model instructed to answer only from provided, retrieved context has much less room to confidently make something up than one relying on parametric memory alone
questions.explanation: Grounding generation in explicit retrieved text — and instructing the model to stick to it — directly counters the tendency of a next-token predictor to produce plausible-sounding but unsupported claims.
